# History of Women’s Rugby World Cup
New Zealand are the most successful team in women’s Rugby World Cup history, having won the title on all six occasions when they have reached the final, in 1998, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2017 and 2021.

New Zealand won the 2017 World Cup, their 5th title.

New Zealand has now won 6 of the 10 tournaments so far.

| 2010 | New Zealand | England | 13-10 | England |
| 2006 | New Zealand | England | 25-17 | Canada |
| 2002 | New Zealand | England | 19-9 | Spain |
| 1998 | New Zealand | USA | 44-12 | Netherlands |

### Tournament Statistics
New Zealand's dominance in the Women's Rugby World Cup is remarkable, having won 6 out of 10 tournaments (60% win rate).

- Most titles: New Zealand (6)

## Frequently Asked Questions
### Which country has won the most Women's Rugby World Cups?
New Zealand has won the most Women's Rugby World Cups with 6 titles out of 10 tournaments.

### Which teams have reached the most World Cup finals?
New Zealand has reached 6 finals and won all of them, demonstrating remarkable efficiency in championship matches.
